findings.text: the fragment cites the graph it read as bolt://98d4-gpu-0002:7687 while the run's own log 01-read.log records bolt://98dci4-gpu-0002:7687, so a reader following the citation to reproduce the read lands on a host that does not exist; the identical mis-citation was raised as a follow-on against the sibling §31 fragment.

the fragment credits the replay's already_applied result to the in-flight plan section §34, but the already_applied recognition path is present on the reviewed base at imas_codex/standard_names/signed_manifest.py:4302 and :4337, so this run demonstrates no §34 behaviour; the same line puts a plan-section label in a durable record, which churns if the plan is renumbered.

receipts_per_name_max falls back to 1 when the receipt map is empty while receipts_per_name_min falls back to 0, so a readback that found no receipts at all would report a maximum of one receipt per name and mislead a reader skimming the pair.

build_row, run and readback duplicate the signed-retirement instrument scaffold of docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/sib-record-orphan-retirements-run.py:86, :263 and :280 without a shared owner module, so the next retirement cohort copies it a third time; no library owner exists for the scaffold, and the authority build itself correctly extends imas_codex/standard_names/repair_authority.py:135.
